newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle expected lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle expected lower.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open 0.100 to 0.250 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle were called off 0.100 to 0.200 cent per lb, livestock analysts said.

Packers have lowered bids for fed cattle following the downward price correction in boxed beef values which should spark carryover selling. Retailers showed heavy resistance to the recent higher boxed beef values and this was expected to curb interest in fed cattle, they said.
Boxed beef cut-out values Tuesday fell $0.88 to $1.96 per cwt, USDA reported.

Expectations the trend in feeder cattle has turned lower after the recent run-up to three-year highs should keep pressure on feeder cattle. Feeder prices are too high for cattle feeders to break even, based on fed cattle prices and the cost of grains, analysts said.
Calls for corn futures were also higher early Wednesday and the latest CME feeder cattle index was lower. This should add to overall pressure, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index slipped $0.25 at $82.31 per cwt.
